meta.strategy: 80/20 by real exam section weights. This file is the objective exam structure (sections, weights, official topics, pass marks, trails, suggested sequences). Per-user personalization — which sections are a candidate's strength vs. gap — is decided interactively by the cert-prep skill, not baked here. Add a new exam by adding one entry under "exams"; the skill and the facilitator dashboard both read this file.

gapLegend.Core: Study hard — high weight and/or commonly missed.
gapLegend.Medium: Medium lift — best-practice judgment or moderate depth.
gapLegend.Verify: Verify, don't re-study — usually home turf for daily practitioners; confirm rather than relearn.

fieldIntel.source: Real passers — Kanani Guyton (tracker F0C301AURRV, Rec0C3SLL7FPC), passed Sep 2026; independently passed by a teammate (Rec0C5EK2FPHN). Hardest section flagged by both: Consent.
hammered: Consent is tied to the Contact Point value (email address or phone number), NOT to the Unified Individual / customer-ID record itself — a Unified Individual can hold multiple contact points, and only opted-in contact points receive a message. Differs from traditional marketing platforms [validated: mktg/264-0-0/mktg_consent_tools_ref.html 'Contact Point' + 'Unified Individual', rel 2]

Consent is powered by Data 360; four objects store consent data: Communication Subscription, Engagement Channel Type, Communication Subscription Channel Type, Communication Subscription Consent [validated: mktg/264-0-0/mktg_consent_tools_ref.html 'Consent Objects', rel 2]

Consent checks are required for promotional email and any SMS/WhatsApp/RCS message; transactional-email consent checks are off by default [validated: mktg/264-0-0/mktg_consent_tools_ref.html 'Consent Check', rel 2]

sections.name: Prompt Engineering
sections.note: Not just writing prompts — access controls, template types, grounding choice, Trust Layer, and model access are all in scope. sections.name: AI Agents
sections.note: The biggest section by far — over a third of the exam. Built around next-gen authoring (Agent Script). Current docs say 'subagents' where the exam guide says 'topics' — expect either term. Canvas view and Script view edit the same Agent Script; Script-view errors can make Canvas view unavailable until fixed [validated: Salesforce Help, Agentforce docs rel 264]. Execution context is heavily testable: Employee agents run as the logged-in user; Service agents run as the agent user unless credential-based user verification is on, and context variables pass identity but do NOT restrict data access [validated: Salesforce Help, Agentforce docs rel 264].

sections.note: Only 5% — know the 'when' and the 'why', not the details. Multi-agent orchestration connects Agentforce agents with other specialized agents in the same org. crossExamCheats.sharedBackbone: Study once, use across exams: DMOs, identity resolution, segmentation, Data 360 provisioning, consumption/credits, and Agentforce grounding concepts. All four exams reward 'agent readiness' — clean metadata, good descriptions, governed access. Agentforce Specialist ⇄ Data 360: the Data 360 Fundamentals section (Data Library, chunking, indexing, retrievers) overlaps with Data 360 grounding/RAG — study once, apply to both.
technique: These are consultant exams: answers favor 'given a scenario, what would you advise' — pick the governed, out-of-box, lowest-maintenance option over the clever custom one.
Watch for Beta-labeled features (e.g. Semantic Model AI Optimization, AI-Generated Descriptions, Inspector proactive alerts) — new exams love testing brand-new features.
105 min / 60 Q = 1:45 per question. Flag and move on; first instinct on scenario questions is usually right.
Wrong-answer patterns: options requiring AMPscript/Apex/custom LLMs (MC Next) or external Tableau Server/Cloud concepts that don't apply to Tableau Next.
